anomalies.observed: The ATO valve path in the netlist is R10 (ATO_VALVE to /G_ATO) driving the gate of T5 (AO3400A, N-channel, drain /D_ATO, pulled down by R12). T3 (AON6407, described as P-Channel) is instead a series element between /+24V_{F} and +24V, with gate /G_RPP biased by R7 and clamped by D3.
anomalies.expected: The specification places T3 (AON6407, described there as an N-MOSFET) as the ATO solenoid low-side switch, with gate driven through R10 and pre-driven by T4, and it lists T5 only as a count in the r1-to-r2 BOM delta. The netlist does not match that role assignment.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives `ATO_VALVE` net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: If the build matches the netlist, the ATO valve is switched by a small AO3400A, not the intended power device, and T3 sits in the 24 V input path as a P-channel element. Actuation and reverse-polarity behaviour would differ from the specification.

anomalies.observed: R5 (10k) connects the main pump gate net /G_{PUMP} to +3V3, not to GND. The other gate pull resistors on the board, R12 on /G_{ATO} and R7 on /G_{RPP}, are not tied to the rail in this way.
anomalies.expected: A 10k gate resistor on a low-side N-MOSFET used for a 24 V pump is normally a pull-down to GND so the pump defaults to off until the controller drives it. A pull-up to 3V3 makes IRLR2905 (logic-level) fully conduct by default, so the main pump runs whenever the ESP32 output is high-impedance, including during boot.
anomalies.impact: The main 24 V circulation pump may energise at power-up or on a controller fault, because the gate is held high by default.

anomalies.observed: The EN pin (pin 2) of the TPS62933 buck regulator U1 has no connection and is flagged as a no-connect. No pull-up or pull-down and no enable net exists on it.
anomalies.expected: A buck regulator's EN pin should be tied to VIN, or through a defined pull resistor, so the converter has a defined enable state; a floating EN pin can leave the 5 V rail off.

evidence.quote: U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A

anomalies.impact: Depending on the part's internal EN default, the +5V rail, the ESP32 and the 3.3 V LDO may never start, or the enable state may be indeterminate.

parsed.summary: The netlist and SPICE deck are internally consistent on values and most connections, so I found no definitive short or value error. The findings are moderate-to-low-confidence concerns: the ATO and pump gate-network roles differ from the specification, the main pump gate is pulled up to 3V3, and the buck regulator's EN pin is floating.
